engineeringSkip.reason: The idea of a wearable 'localized ionic shield' that filters air around a person is not based on known physics; electrostatic precipitation requires collection surfaces and cannot form a protective bubble.

factCheck.reason: Ions do not form a protective bubble around a wearer — electrostatic precipitation only cleans air that is actively drawn past charged collection plates, so a collar cannot filter 99% of pollutants and pathogens out of the open air around a person.
